title: Mock 5 · Tax, Ethics & Revision
blurb: A revision round with extra focus on taxation, distributor ethics and the new 2026 additions (PaRRVA, CSCRF, MF Regulations 2026).

questions.q: The additional compensation an investor demands over the nominal risk-free rate for uncertainty in future cash flows is called:
questions.explanation: If returns are uncertain, the additional compensation over the risk-free rate is the risk premium; higher risk, higher premium.
hints: Wrong: alpha is excess return from skill/unsystematic risk.
Wrong: that is pure time value of money.
Wrong: inflation compensation is already in the nominal rate.

questions.q: Which of the following is a real (physical) asset rather than a financial asset?
questions.explanation: Box 1.1 lists gold, diamonds, precious metals and real estate as physical assets; shares, debentures, deposits, PPF and MF investments are financial assets.
hints: Correct: gold is a physical asset.

questions.q: A shareholder holding 200 shares receives a bonus issue in the ratio 1:4. How many bonus shares does he get?
questions.explanation: A 1:4 bonus gives 1 bonus share for every 4 held: 200 / 4 = 50 shares.
hints: Wrong: that would be a 1:1 bonus.
Wrong: that would be a 1:5 bonus.

questions.q: A company's enterprise value is ₹500 crore, its debt is ₹150 crore and it holds cash of ₹30 crore. The intrinsic value of equity is:
questions.explanation: Equity value = EV - Debt + Cash = 500 - 150 + 30 = ₹380 crore.
hints: Wrong: subtracts cash instead of adding.

questions.q: In the FCFE model, the free cash flows are discounted at the:
options: Cost of equity, typically from CAPM
Coupon rate on the company's bonds
questions.explanation: FCFE is discounted using the cost of equity (re), derived from CAPM; FCFF uses WACC.
hints: Wrong: not a discount rate for equity cash flows.

questions.q: A forward (leading) P/E ratio is computed by dividing the current market price by:
options: The sum of the last four quarters' EPS
The sum of the expected EPS of the next four quarters
questions.explanation: Trailing P/E uses the last four quarters' EPS; forward P/E uses the expected EPS of the next four quarters.
hints: Wrong: that gives the inverse of dividend yield.

questions.q: Which statement about credit ratings is correct as per the workbook?
options: Ratings are given to a firm, so all its instruments share one rating
A higher credit rating means higher default risk
Ratings are given to an instrument, so two instruments of the same firm can have different ratings
Modifiers + and - can be used with AAA and D
questions.explanation: Rating is given for an instrument and not to a firm. Higher rating means lower default risk. Modifiers apply to AA through C for long-term instruments.
hints: Wrong: higher rating means lower default risk.
Wrong: modifiers apply to AA to C only.

questions.q: In a PMS, the total exposure of a client in derivatives:
options: Can be up to twice the portfolio value
Should not exceed the client's portfolio value
Is unlimited if the client agrees
Must be at least 25% of the portfolio
questions.explanation: The total exposure of a client in derivatives should not exceed the client's portfolio value; PMs cannot leverage client portfolios for derivatives.

questions.q: The September 2026 workbook cites which regulations for the definition of a mutual fund (which now covers silver-related instruments too)?
questions.explanation: The 2026 workbook quotes the SEBI (Mutual Fund) Regulations, 2026 definition: a trust raising money through units for investing in securities, money market instruments, gold/silver related instruments and other assets.
hints: Wrong: the workbook now cites the 2026 regulations.

questions.q: A client redeems ₹30 lakh from his PMS in the third year of investment. The maximum exit load the PM may charge is:
questions.explanation: In the third year the cap is 1% of the amount redeemed: 1% x ₹30 lakh = ₹30,000.
hints: Wrong: nil applies only after three years.

questions.q: The ₹50 lakh minimum investment requirement does NOT apply to:
options: Accredited investors, subject to disclosures and agreed terms
questions.explanation: Subject to disclosures in the disclosure document and agreed terms, the minimum investment does not apply to accredited investors (nor to co-investment PMs).

questions.q: Which of the following is listed among the DON'Ts for portfolio managers?
options: Leveraging the portfolio of clients for investment in derivatives
Abiding by the Code of Conduct
Keeping client funds in a Scheduled Commercial Bank
questions.explanation: The PM shall not leverage the portfolio of its clients for investment in derivatives. The other options are DO's.

questions.q: Portfolio managers must have an automated system with minimal manual intervention for order management and allocation (for equity and MF units) when their AUM is:
questions.explanation: PMs with AUM of INR 1,000 crore or more under discretionary and non-discretionary services must have an automated system.

questions.q: In a jointly held PMS account, investment records are created and benefits such as dividends and redemption proceeds are paid to:
questions.explanation: Records are created in the name of the first holder and all benefits are paid to the first holder's account.

questions.q: Which rule applies to the dealing team of a portfolio manager?
options: Dealers may use personal mobile phones for speed
Any employee may enter the dealing room
Conversations only through dedicated recorded lines or authorised email IDs
questions.explanation: All DT conversations must be via recorded lines or authorised emails; mobile phones are not allowed; access and internet are restricted.
hints: Wrong: mobile phones are not allowed.
Wrong: entry is restricted to authorised employees.
Wrong: internet is restricted to trade execution.

questions.q: In investor profiling, the time period for which investments are proposed to be made with the portfolio manager must be:
options: The same as the term of the agreement
questions.explanation: The workbook notes that the time period proposed with the PM has to be the same as the term of the agreement.
hints: Wrong: it is a client-agreement matter.
Correct: same as the agreement term.

questions.q: APMI prescribes a maximum of how many benchmarks for each strategy?
questions.explanation: APMI shall prescribe a maximum of three benchmarks for each strategy; the PM selects one of them for the IA.
hints: Wrong: up to three are prescribed.

questions.q: An investor owns assets with a market value of ₹2 crore and has loans outstanding of ₹50 lakh. His net worth is:
questions.explanation: Net worth = assets at market value - liabilities = ₹2 crore - ₹0.5 crore = ₹1.5 crore.

questions.q: The factor that targets stocks undervalued relative to fundamentals, such as low P/E or P/B, is:
questions.explanation: The value factor holds that stocks undervalued relative to fundamentals (low P/E or P/B) tend to outperform over time.
hints: Wrong: low volatility targets low price fluctuation.

questions.q: A portfolio returned 15% with a beta of 1.2 when the risk-free rate was 6%. Its Treynor ratio is:
questions.explanation: Treynor = (Rp - Rf) / β = (15 - 6) / 1.2 = 7.5 (percentage points per unit of beta).
hints: Wrong: return / beta without subtracting Rf.

questions.q: Which is a criterion of a good benchmark as per the workbook?
options: It should be secret so that managers cannot game it
It should be investable, allowing passive exposure
It should have a higher risk than the portfolio
Its constituents may change without disclosure
questions.explanation: A good benchmark has clearly defined constituents and weights, is investable, consistent with the approach, has the same risk-return profile and is measurable.
hints: Wrong: constituents must be clearly defined.
Wrong: constituents and weights must be clearly defined.

questions.q: PMS fees attract GST at the rate of:
questions.explanation: PMS fees attract 18% GST, which increases cost and is not deductible from taxable income.

questions.q: An NRI who wishes to trade in F&O through a PMS in India must use:
options: An NRO account, on a non-repatriable basis
An NRE account, on a repatriable basis
questions.explanation: NRIs can trade F&O through PMS using their NRO account (non-repatriable); they cannot use the NRE account for F&O trading.
hints: Wrong: NRE cannot be used for F&O.
Wrong: NRIs cannot use resident accounts.

questions.q: Under Section 12 of PMLA, records of documents evidencing identity of clients must be maintained for:
options: 2 years after the account is closed
5 years after the business relationship has ended or the account closed, whichever is later
questions.explanation: Identity records shall be maintained for five years after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later.
hints: Correct: 5 years after closure/ending, whichever later.

questions.q: As per the 2026 workbook, SEBI-regulated entities must report cyber incidents through the designated SEBI email within:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandated REs to report cyber incidents through mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours and on the SEBI Incident Reporting Portal within 24 hours.
hints: Wrong: 24 hours is for the Incident Reporting Portal.
Wrong: that is the STR timeline.
Wrong: that is the grievance timeline.
